verdicts.opus: B and D both grounded every number in the single news.compare call, and A and C produced no measurements. D read the data more carefully: it named the spike months and computed critical shares. It also caught that the tool's direction labels contradict the endpoints, whereas B's verdict misstated the direction of onion coverage. D's weaknesses are a selected-months chart that drops the wheat spike and a verdict that restates the direction labels it had just questioned.
verdicts.gpt: A is the strongest decision aid: it compares all three terms on one traced window, gives a complete monthly series and reproducible ratios, and distinguishes media attention from price movement. B adds useful spike observations but has material window, coverage, and overlap errors; C and D are transparent about missing measurements but do not answer the comparison.
